name: Fajita Chicken Rice Bowl
intro_html: A high-protein, low-fat Tex-Mex chicken, rice, black bean, and pepper meal prep. Fourteen servings at about {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein for roughly ${{cost_ps}} each (at everyday cost).
ingredients_display: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 5.5 lb raw (2495 g)
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast, 5.5 lb raw: ~$12.27. Buy 6 lbs: $13.38.
Rice, 4 cups dry jasmine: ~$0.99. Buy 1 (lasts several batches).
Yellow Onion, 1 small onion, sliced: ~$0.75. Buy 1 lb: $1.14.
Pantry seasonings (fajita seasoning): ~$4.30. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $30.36 across 14 servings, so roughly $2.17 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $32.62 across 14 servings, roughly $2.33 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $6.25 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $38.87. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: That's about ${{cost_ps}} a bowl (at everyday cost), versus $10 or more for a single fast-casual fajita bowl.
shop_smart: Buy chicken when it's on sale, then freeze it. Stores drop chicken to a sale price at random. We recently grabbed 50 lbs on a deep markdown instead of our usual shelf price and loaded the deep freezer. At about 5.5 lbs per batch, that one buy makes about 9 batches, or roughly 63 nights of dinner for two.

The seasoning is your priciest line per ounce. Six Taco Bell packets are what drives that. A store-brand fajita or taco seasoning is a fraction of the cost, and mixing your own from chili powder, cumin, paprika, garlic, and onion powder costs pennies. Just know the macros shift a little if you swap.
Buy rice in the big bag. A 25-lb bag of jasmine is far cheaper per pound than a small box. Compare the price per ounce. That's the number that tells you the real deal.
Beans by the case, peppers in season. Canned beans are cheapest bought a case at a time, and bell peppers drop hard when they're in season or in a 3-count bag. Frozen pepper strips work too.
make_it: Weigh your empty pot first. Put the largest pot you'll use to mix everything onto your large scale and write down its weight. You'll need that number at the end to portion accurately.
Cook the rice (4 cups dry jasmine plus water per the package) and set aside.
Slice the bell peppers and yellow onion into strips.
Cube the chicken breast and cook it in a large skillet with the olive oil until done.
Add the fajita seasoning with a splash of water, toss in the peppers and onion, and simmer until they soften and everything is coated.
Combine the rice, seasoned chicken and vegetables, and beans back in the big pot and stir.
portion_html: Set the full pot on your large scale and subtract the empty-pot weight you noted in Step 1. That's your total food weight. Divide it by 14, then scoop that amount into each glass container. Every bowl lands right at about {{cal}} cal and {{protein}}g protein.
upsell_html: Two weeks of high-protein dinners for about ${{cost_ps}} a bowl (at everyday cost). This is one of many. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money, work, and life lessons, all for $1 a month.
